September 16 37.

My dear Steptoe,

Further to my letter dated June 14, 1937,
I have to state that efforts to locate the relative
of Miss Yeung Teh Yun(楊德雲), a communist suspect,
have been made but without result. It was anticipated
that Miss Yeung Teh Yun would return to Great China
University to resume her studies in September, 1937,
but since the re-opening of this school has been
postponed indefinitely, further inquiries regarding
this suspect are impossible.

Yours sincerely,

M. M. Steptoe, Esq.,
H.B.M. Consulate-General,
Shanghai.

SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL POLICE.    File No............
S.1, Special Branch. xxxxx,
REPORT
Date September 16, 1937.

Subject (in full) Miss Yeung Teh Yun, a communist suspect.

Made by Clerk Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by C. Gandon D.C.

With reference to the remarks of D.C. (Special Branch)
on the attached report, I beg to state that efforts have
been made to locate the relative of Miss Yeung Teh Yun,
a communist suspect, but without result. It was intended
to further the enquiries at the beginning of September, 1937,
when the Great China University, Chung San Road, was scheduled
to re-open and Miss Yeung Teh Yun would return to resume her
studies but because of the present hostilities the reopening
has been postponed indefinitely and enquiries are therefore
at present nullified.

Liao Chung Chien.
Clerk

D.C. (Crime & Special Branches).

（批：D.B.R. 16/9.）

Subject Letter from British Consulate-General re a communist suspect
named Yeung Teh Yun (楊德雲).

Made by Clerk Liao Chung Chien Forwarded by J. Byrne D.S.I

Discreet enquiries have been made regarding Yeung Teh
Yun and it has been ascertained that the person is a girl
and not a man.

Miss Yeung is a native of Kweichow, age 16 years, at
present studying in the Junior 3rd Class of the Middle
School Department of the Great China University, Chung San
Road, and staying at the Kwang Ying Tsai (群英齋), which is
the name for the Girl Students Quarters of the University.
She joined the school in February, 1937, and gave her
native address as follows:-
Bah Yang Zai, Kiang Lung, Chennin Hsien, Kweichow.
(貴州 鎮寧 江龍白楊寨)

(批：Perhaps useful to locate her relatives for security)
(印：SPECIAL BRANCH SHANGHAI S.M.P. 14 JUNE 1937)

Miss Yeung claimed to have some relatives in Shanghai and
when on holidays she has stayed in their home. No one in
the school, however, knows where her relatives reside.

Miss Yeung has the appearance of a common Chinese country
maid. A brief description of hers is as follows:-
Age 16; Height about 4' 8"; Medium build;
Dark yellow complexion; Face round and with freckles;
Straight bobbed hair; Often wears clothes made of
cotton cloth; Does not use powder and rouge.

She is not very bright in her studies and is unsociable.
Nothing can be learned from her attitude and habits.
Realising her inability, she did not participate in
this term's final examination which is still in progress.
On June 7, she left the school telling her classmates that she
was going to stay with her relatives for a few days. She did
not return to school until June 11, 1937.

主题 英国总领事馆关于名为杨德云（楊德雲）的共党嫌疑犯的来信。

由 书记员 廖仲坚 撰写 经由 J. Byrne 副督察长 转呈

经对杨德云进行秘密查询，查明该人为女性而非男性。

杨小姐籍贯贵州，年龄16岁，目前在中山路大夏大学中学部初中三年级就读，住宿于“群英斋”，即该校女生宿舍。她于1937年2月入学，登记的籍贯地址如下：
贵州镇宁江龙白杨寨。
(貴州 鎮寧 江龍白楊寨)

（批：或许有助于定位其亲属以确保安全）
（印：上海公共租界工部局警务处 特务科 1937年6月14日）

杨小姐声称在上海有一些亲属，假期时曾住在他们家中。然而，校内无人知晓其亲属居住何处。

杨小姐外表看似普通的中国乡村女仆。其简要描述如下：
年龄16岁；身高约4英尺8英寸；中等身材；
暗黄色皮肤；圆脸且有雀斑；
直发短发；常穿棉布衣服；不施粉黛。

她学业并不聪颖，且不喜社交。从其态度和习惯中看不出什么名堂。鉴于自知能力不足，她未参加本学期仍在进行的期末考试。6月7日，她离开学校，告诉同学说要去亲戚家住几天。直到1937年6月11日她才返回学校。

A copy of her test papers, dated 14/5/37, has been secured
and when compared with the letters intercepted by the Hongkong
authorities (photostatic copies) it reveals that there are
a number of dissimilarities between Miss Yeung's penmanship
and that of the writer of the letters. In view of this

by members of the Communist Party as well as other secret
societies to communicate through a third person whose address and
employment would not arouse suspicion. A photostatic copy
of one of Miss Yeung's papers is attached herewith.
Enquiries are still proceeding and further information

TRANSLATION

Messrs. Yen Tsz and Yung Sz (雁子 永思 ),
A fortnight has elapsed since I left you, and I
trust that you are in good health.
Not long after my arrival in Shanghai, I met Mr.
Sun(遜气). Apart from our business conversation,
we often talked about your wholehearted assistance in
all our affairs. Undoubtedly our affairs gave you
quite unnecessary anxiety. What we can never forget
is the faithful advice and enco...ment you have given
us. These sympathetic expressions have of course made
a deep impression on us. Really, if we stayed with
you a long time, we would be afforded a natural opportunity
to increase our knowledge and experience.
We stayed at your home for about two months. During
this period, we were always arguing and quarrelling over
trifling private affairs. This procedure unquestionably
caused great inconvenience to your family. Indeed, we can
hardly recollect without shame our reckless behaviour □□
which is really "That" (Translator's note ; this expression was
recently introduced into Chinese conversation, letter-
writing, and fiction, and means indescribable). I feel
very ashamed.
Nevertheless I trust you fully realise the fiery
temper of the youth, and consequently I ask your forgive-
ness.
After my arrival in Shanghai, I intended to write
you, but owing to the pressing nature of numerous petty
affairs I have delayed it to the present. Of course
my laziness is also to blame, but anyway I hope you will
excuse me.

雁子、永思 二位先生：

自别后已逾两旬，想必二位安康。
抵沪不久，即遇孙先生（遜气）。除商务交谈外，我们常谈及二位对我们各项事务的全心协助。毫无疑问，我们的事务令二位颇费不必要的焦虑。我们永难忘怀的是二位给予我们的忠告与鼓励（enco...ment原文残缺）。这些同情之辞自然给我们留下了深刻印象。确实，若我们与二位久居，将获得增长见识与经验的天然机会。
我们在府上逗留约两个月。在此期间，我们常因琐碎私事争论吵闹。此举无疑给贵府带来极大不便。的确，回想我们当时的鲁莽行为□□，不禁羞愧难当，这真是“那个”（译者注：此表达最近引入中文会话、书信及小说中，意为难以形容）。我感到非常惭愧。
尽管如此，我相信二位充分理解青年人的火爆脾气，因此恳请二位原谅。
抵沪后，我本欲致信，但因众多琐事紧迫，拖延至今。当然，我的懒惰也是原因之一，但无论如何，希望二位能谅解。

其他人已离开香港，且您将房屋租予他人。宋先生和我对此变故感到非常惊讶。不知缘由何在。
离港前我曾与您交谈；您是否仍不愿相信我们？
宋先生将于这一两天南下。或许，我不久也将前往南方。若您尚未出租房屋，那么我们抵达时将省去许多麻烦。若已租予他人，则无可奈何，我们抵达香港后再解决此事。

pages.en:
TRANSLATION

Yung: 之.

Your second letter by air mail was received to-day.
At the beginning I want to say this to you "We
must examine everything coolly: If it is not necessary
to settle a matter in a rash manner, we must patiently
find some slow way of settling it." If you would
permit me, I would say that you are slightly insane.
I can tell you openly that the task you entrusted
me with has been accomplished with fair success. I am
not boasting. I am only showing that I am still very
loyal to you. Your letter, however, which I have just
received, was full of disappointment with my work,
conveying the impression that somebody here is joking
with you.
One or two days after your departure, I already
thought of sending a letter to Hongkong to inform you
of the situation here. But, you know, how contradictory
a human being's feelings are. So I delayed the posting
of the letter until I received your first letter from
Hongkong on April 24, and I then sent out the reply on
April 25. With regard to the publication, as soon as
I received it from Mr. Wong(王 ) and returned home,
I posted it (April 19). I may say that I have carried
out your affairs. So I say "Don't be so quick tempered";
you see, these affairs cannot be accomplished as soon
as the thoughts strike you. The facts show how hasty
you are. The airmail from Hongkong does not arrive
everyday, and sometimes is delayed for a number of days.
I think you realize this. Again you say that the air-
mail is on the contrary slower than the ordinary mail
from Shanghai. This is a mistake. In fact, the air-mail
is quicker.
pages.zh:
译文

永：之。

今日收到您的第二封航空邮件。
开头我想对您说：“我们必须冷静审视一切：若无需仓促解决某事，我们必须耐心寻找缓慢解决之道。”若您允许，我要说您略显疯狂。
我可以坦率地告诉您，您委托我的任务已取得相当成功的进展。我并非自夸。我只是表明我对您依然非常忠诚。然而，我刚收到的您的来信，充满了对我的工作失望之情，给人一种此处有人在与您开玩笑的印象。
您离开后的一两天，我就想过写信到香港告知您这里的情况。但是，您知道，人的感情是多么矛盾。所以我延迟了发信，直到4月24日收到您从香港寄来的第一封信，随后于4月25日发出回信。关于出版事宜，我一从王（Wong）先生处拿到稿件回家，就将其寄出（4月19日）。我可以说我已经办理了您的事务。所以我说“不要如此急躁”；您看，这些事务不可能念头一动就立刻完成。事实表明您多么草率。香港的航空邮件并非每天到达，有时会延误数天。我想您明白这一点。您又说航空邮件反而比上海的普通邮件慢。这是错误的。事实上，航空邮件更快。

pages.en:
-2-
You ask me for travelling expenses. After
thorough consideration, I feel quite uneasy. I fully
realize your hardship, and do you think that when you
are in need of money I intentionally say such distaste-
ful words? But you must understand the situation. I
will do my best to arrange for some money. At present,
I can only obtain $5 but what is the use of such a small
sum to you.
Mr. Sung has already left for the South and in a
few days you may see him. Of course at that time,
do you think that he will disregard all your desires?
Besides, it is still doubtful whether I can get the $5.
Frankly speaking, it is very difficult to get money
these days. Wait for a few days until I have found
some means and then I will not speak of $5 but of a
round sum. I am not joking.
I strongly oppose your back sliding. A youth
should not be like that. Lack of determination shows
our weakness. If you were at Shanghai at present, I
would surely give you a nice lesson by beating you.
My dear, wait for me at Hongkong, as I am coming
south soon. How intimate is our friendship? Can we
say that your desire to come to Shanghai is just to be
by my side? Control your feelings, we will soon see
each other.
Where are you staying now? Is it really so
difficult to obtain a livelihood? Don't ask assistance
from them. Sell your things, and pawn your clothes
to maintain yourself, until I can find some way to
secure funds for your relief. Don't be discouraged, but
do your best to resist the enemy! Let me stop here;
now don't say again that you want to return to Shanghai.
With best regards,
pages.zh:
-2-
您向我索要旅费。经过深思熟虑，我感到十分不安。我充分理解您的困境，您是否认为在您急需金钱时，我故意说这些令人不快的话？但您必须理解现状。我将尽力安排一些资金。目前，我只能弄到5元，但这区区小钱对您有何用处。
宋先生已南下，过几天您或许能见到他。当然，届时您认为他会无视您的所有愿望吗？此外，我能否拿到这5元尚存疑问。坦白说，如今弄钱非常困难。再等几天，待我找到办法，那时我说的就不是5元，而是一笔整数。我不是在开玩笑。
我强烈反对您的退缩。青年人不应如此。缺乏决心显示了我们的软弱。若您此刻在上海，我定会通过痛打您来给您一个深刻的教训。
亲爱的，在香港等我，因为我很快就要南下。我们的友谊多么亲密？难道能说您想来上海只是为了在我身边吗？控制您的情绪，我们很快就会见面。
您现在住在哪里？谋生真的如此艰难吗？不要向他们求助。变卖物品，典当衣物以维持生计，直到我找到办法筹集资金救济您。不要气馁，但要尽力抵抗敌人！就此搁笔；现在不要再说要回上海了。
此致
敬礼

Yours Sincerely,
Hulton
